prompt: Ben revises the content for his science test thoroughly, but his teacher's comments keep saying the same thing: the question asked him to 'explain' and he only 'described'. What is the most useful change to his practice?

options.text: Revise the content for longer, since knowing more will automatically fix his answers
Write faster in the test, so he has time to add extra detail at the end
In practice questions, underline the command word first and plan an answer that does what it asks — reasons and links for 'explain', not just features
Memorise longer definitions, because 'explain' questions mainly reward length

explanation: Ben's gap is not knowledge but matching his answer to the question. Noticing the command word and practising the type of answer it demands — explanation means saying why, not just what — targets the marks he is actually losing.
